# Headless gather, summary

Labelling rule, stated as the harness's own and read from the app's own selection and the record's sentence. IR-SCIENCE.md 4b-ix (the vegetation axis) says: "Model the white-balanced red channel as a visible part plus an infrared part and green as infrared alone; then the difference `d = R - G` over `G`". Source line: IR-SCIENCE.md section 4b-ix, first paragraph; section 6 says to split first, measure each, and carry the population not asked about as the control.
- A thinned pixel is sky when the app's own sky selection (the refined bitmap, the coarse one when there is none; src/skyfine.ts buildSkySelectionFrom) reads at least 0.5 at its position. The weight is the harness's own figure.
- Otherwise it is neutral when its saturation at the opening render (the swap on, the opening balance, the page's own floor 0.13) is under that floor.
- Otherwise it is foliage when (R - G) / G, taken from the linear camera values times the opening gains, is at most -0.05 (the harness's own sign and threshold: foliage on the negative side, where green infrared alone exceeds the red the visible part has lowered). Otherwise it is other.
- Every count is also kept for all pixels as the whole-frame population. Hue is the HSV hue of the 8-bit display P3 pixel the drawn path ends with, in 72 bins of 5 degrees, counted over pixels at or above the floor 0.13; saturation and lightness are in 10 bands of one tenth, lightness being Rec.709 luma of the 8-bit values. The chroma plane is CIE chroma and hue from the same 8-bit values read through the sRGB transfer and primaries, counted over chroma at or above 5; reading P3 values through sRGB is a measuring convention, not a claim.
- Differences from the editor: the frame is the plain decode without the lens flat; no lens curve; the computed path (compileEdit) with the sRGB to P3 conversion applied after 8-bit rounding, not the GPU; the pixels are every k-th pixel of every k-th row of the half-size decode as the page thins them.
